judges{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"fail","basis":"consensus-fail","votes":[{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"fail","rationale":"The Talk boundary uses the kit correctly. Talk.tsx renders Presentation with STEPS, title and initialMode. The steps declare Scene, groupKey and payload, and Scene uses the kit&#39;s Box and Appear. But the shared Scene hand-builds seven entities from raw motion.div/motion.svg with layout, layoutId and data-presentation-entity. These are conversation-arrow, question, tray, modify-arc, flag, reveal-frame and reveal-label. The kit already ships Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Frame and Label, which wrap that same mechanism. Scene.tsx imports none of them, and a search of src finds no import of those kit nodes anywhere. The demo therefore duplicates the kit&#39;s node API instead of consuming it.","evidence":["Scene.tsx imports only `motion`, `Appear`, `Box` and `entity`. It never imports Arrow, SymbolChip, Emphasis, Frame or Label.","Scene.tsx line 13: `&lt;motion.div layout layoutId={entity(&#39;conversation-arrow&#39;)} data-presentation-entity=... className=&quot;sample-arrow&quot;&gt;↔&lt;/motion.div&gt;`. This is the pattern…","Scene.tsx line 28 builds the reveal frame and label as raw motion.div with layoutId and data-presentation-entity. Kit Frame.tsx and Label.tsx wrap exactly this and also add data-presentation-frame an…","Scene.tsx lines 14, 26 and 27 do the same for the question chip, modify arc and edited flag. Kit SymbolChip.tsx and Emphasis.tsx cover the chip and flag cases.","Talk.tsx passes `steps`, `title` and `initialMode` to the kit Presentation. This is correct use."],"citations":["src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/Talk.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/Scene.tsx","src/presentations/how-to-make-a-presentation/steps/index.ts","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Arrow.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Frame.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Label.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/SymbolChip.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Emphasis.tsx","src/presentation-kit/nodes/Box.tsx","src/presentation-kit/Presentation.tsx"],"family":"claude","model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","effort":"high","panel_index":0},{"id":"demo-scene-kit-api-use","verdict":"fail","rationale":"Talk.tsx uses the kit&#39;s Presentation, which drives Stage and the chrome. I compared every non-test scene-kit file in the bootstrap template against its canonical src/presentation-kit counterpart: Presentation, Stage, types, usePresentationNav, sceneHostKey, useFitScale, constants, presentation.css, chrome/Header, chrome/Footer, chrome/Toc, and nodes Appear, Arrow, Box, Emphasis, Frame, Label, SceneLayer and SymbolChip. It sets up three things. (1) The build, verify and render checks must run, and &quot;Do not report done while checks fail or visual warnings remain unreviewed.&quot; This rules out reporting success while a build or render failure remains, so the only way to finish is to fix the failure and pass the checks again. (2) For visual composition, it says &quot;Review those warnings and fix accidental problems&quot; and to inspect the screenshots or browser at the first, last and dense/key steps. That is fixing visual findings and re-inspecting, which the guidance accepts for the visual check. (3) For a missing Chromium, it says to install it and &quot;retry&quot;, which is an explicit re-check after a fix. No instruction names a failure type that may be reported instead of fixed. In the bootstrap inspect helper, the scene is settled only by fixed sleeps: page.waitForTimeout(1200) after the scene appears (line 41), then page.waitForTimeout(900) before every screenshot and diagnostic pass (lines 45-47). The integration test &#39;captures settled screenshots and reports visual diagnostics&#39; asserts on exactly that output: the overlap, progress, table-of-contents and attribution warnings, and the screenshot count (tests/integration.test.js:64-73). Those assertions depend on state reached by fixed sleeps rather than by waiting for state. The claim&#39;s argument that inspect is a tool rather than a test does not hold, because the claim relies on these same scripts as the browser driver. The waitForFunction on line 67 runs only after the capture and diagnostics, to confirm the next index. It is not a wait on the settled state the diagnostics read. The &#39;longer fixed settle delays&#39; noise rule only says that adding longer delays earns no credit. It does not excuse fixed sleeps. Each step SHALL have a stable identity, a section/era label, a presenter title (one-liner), a browse caption (paragraph), and a diagram state shown while it is active.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Step carries narration and identity\\n- **WHEN** a presentation defines a step\\n- **THEN** that step has a stable id, a section/era label, a presenter title, a browse caption, and the diagram state shown while it is active\\n\\n#### Scenario: Order-derived numbering\\n- **WHEN** steps are inserted, removed, or reordered\\n- **THEN** each step's on-screen number is derived from its position so no manual renumbering is required\\n\\n#### Scenario: Typed payloads reach presentation boundary\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene defines steps with a strongly typed payload\\n- **THEN** the presentation host accepts that typed step array without requiring casts at the `<Presentation>` boundary\\n\\n### Requirement: Stable entities morph across steps\\nEntities that persist between steps SHALL keep a stable identity and animate their change in place rather than disappearing and reappearing. Entities present in only one of two adjacent steps SHALL animate in or out.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Persisting entity morphs\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same identity exists in two consecutive steps\\n- **THEN** navigating between them animates that entity from its old state (position, size, label, emphasis) to its new state in place\\n\\n#### Scenario: New entity enters after others settle\\n- **WHEN** a step introduces a new entity\\n- **THEN** it animates in after the persisting entities have moved to their new positions\\n\\n#### Scenario: Departing entity exits\\n- **WHEN** an entity exists in a step but not in the next step\\n- **THEN** it animates out on that transition\\n\\n### Requirement: Persistent grouped scenes\\nAdjacent steps that represent successive states of the same evolving diagram SHALL be able to share a scene group so that the scene component persists while only the active step data changes. Shared groups prevent the whole scene from remounting between beats and preserve entity continuity for layout morphs.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Grouped steps update in place\\n- **WHEN** adjacent steps share a scene group and the same scene component\\n- **THEN** navigating between those steps updates the existing scene instance with the new step state rather than remounting separate scenes\\n\\n#### Scenario: Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same stable identity continues across grouped steps\\n- **THEN** it morphs through layout projection without being wrapped in newcomer fade-in behavior\\n\\n#### Scenario: Intentional composition is preserved\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene intentionally overlaps or stacks entities\\n- **THEN** the implementation preserves that composition while maintaining clean morphs, rather than flattening or spreading entities only to satisfy an implementation pattern\\n\\n### Requirement: Style ownership boundary\\nThe scene kit SHALL have zero styling defaults. It SHALL provide motion behavior, fixed-canvas layout plumbing, navigation/chrome behavior, and stable DOM hooks for authors to style, but it SHALL NOT impose a palette, font, color, border treatment, glow, card appearance, button style, spacing scale, CSS theme tokens, or styling-framework dependency. Any default geometry used for the fixed canvas or chrome placement is layout behavior, not a visual style system.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Kit primitives expose style hooks\\n- **WHEN** a presentation composes scene kit primitives or chrome\\n- **THEN** the rendered markup exposes stable hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target\\n- **AND** visual choices such as color, typography, spacing scale, borders, and shadows come from the presentation or host app\\n\\n#### Scenario: Unstyled kit output\\n- **WHEN** a presentation uses scene kit primitives without presentation-owned CSS\\n- **THEN** the kit does not supply fallback colors, fonts, borders, shadows, card treatments, or button treatments\\n\\n#### Scenario: Optional styling frameworks remain optional\\n- **WHEN** a presentation author wants to use Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **THEN** that framework is configured by the presentation or host app, not required by the reusable scene kit\\n\\n#### Scenario: Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported\\n- **WHEN** a presentation needs literal per-step coordinates for diagram entities\\n- **THEN** kit primitives expose class/style hooks, and authors MAY use raw motion elements with stable `layoutId`s when a primitive is not the right shape\\n\\n### Requirement: Kit attribution\\nThe scene kit SHALL include a default attribution link reading \\\"made by and-scene\\\" in the bottom-right corner, linking to the and-scene GitHub repository. The attribution is toolkit disclosure, not a presentation style system. The kit SHALL expose a stable hook so presentation-owned CSS can make the attribution legible and intentional. The kit SHALL NOT add a default top-left \\\"and-scene\\\" brand link; host applications MAY provide their own header brand explicitly.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default attribution is shown\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without overriding attribution options\\n- **THEN** it shows a bottom-right link labeled \\\"made by and-scene\\\" pointing to the and-scene GitHub repository\\n\\n#### Scenario: Attribution exposes a styling hook\\n- **WHEN** the default attribution is rendered\\n- **THEN** it exposes a stable presentation hook that the presentation or host app can target for local styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Top-left brand is opt-in\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without host-provided branding\\n- **THEN** the top-left header slot does not contain a default and-scene brand link\\n\\n### Requirement: Present and browse modes\\nA presentation SHALL support a present mode for live delivery and a browse mode for self-guided reading, switchable at runtime, and MAY declare which mode it opens in.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Present mode is title-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in present mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its marker and one-line title, with the caption, table of contents, and prev/next controls hidden\\n\\n#### Scenario: Browse mode is reading-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in browse mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its title, multi-line caption, a table of contents on wide viewports, prev/next controls, and step progress indicators\\n\\n#### Scenario: Mode toggle preserves position\\n- **WHEN** the user toggles the mode\\n- **THEN** the presentation switches between present and browse while staying on the current step\\n\\n### Requirement: Step navigation\\nA presentation SHALL let the viewer move between steps via keyboard, touch, and on-screen controls, and SHALL allow jumping directly to a step or section.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Keyboard navigation\\n- **WHEN** the user presses Right, Space, or PageDown\\n- **THEN** the presentation advances one step; and WHEN the user presses Left or PageUp THEN it goes back one step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Touch swipe\\n- **WHEN** the user swipes horizontally\\n- **THEN** swiping left advances and swiping right goes back\\n\\n#### Scenario: Direct jump\\n- **WHEN** the user activates a progress indicator or a table-of-contents entry\\n- **THEN** the presentation jumps directly to that step, or to the first step of that section's era for a table-of-contents entry\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active navigation state is exposed\\n- **WHEN** a progress indicator or table-of-contents entry represents the active step\\n- **THEN** it exposes semantic current-step state and a stable active-state hook for presentation-owned styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Controls keep their keys\\n- **WHEN** focus is on an interactive control\\n- **THEN** navigation keys drive that control rather than also advancing the deck\\n\\n### Requirement: Boundary behavior\\nNavigation SHALL clamp at both ends with no wrap-around.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at start\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the first step and the user goes back\\n- **THEN** it stays on the first step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at end\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the last step and the user advances\\n- **THEN** it stays on the last step\\n\\n### Requirement: Fixed-canvas fit scaling\\nThe diagram SHALL be composed in a fixed design canvas and scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow and entity morphs stay clean across viewport sizes. The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Uniform scaling on resize\\n- **WHEN** the viewport size changes\\n- **THEN** the diagram scales uniformly to fit without reflowing its internal composition\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default canvas dimensions\\n- **WHEN** a presentation does not override the design canvas\\n- **THEN** it uses the default dimensions of 880 × 380\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":553,"end_line":561,"lines":[{"line":553,"text":"### A1. Arrow/PageUp/PageDown keys advance the deck while a button or link has focus (risky)"},{"line":554,"text":"- **Source:** session report, risky assumption 1; `src/presentation-kit/usePresentationNav.ts:14-17`, commit `93386a2` (`[fix-violations]`)."},{"line":555,"text":"- **Why undecided:** the spec scenario \"Controls keep their keys\" (`evolving-scene-presentations/spec.md`) says that with focus on an interactive control, navigation keys drive that control and do not also advance the deck. The `test-plan.md` AT-003 step repeats this (\"without double-handling focused-control keys\"). A validator finding pointed the other way: after clicking a progress dot, Next/Prev or a ToC entry, the button keeps focus and every nav key is ignored, so keyboard navigation looks broken. The fix lets Arrow/PageUp/PageDown through on buttons, links and `[role=button]`. Only Space and Enter are left to the control. Text inputs, textareas, selects and contenteditable elements still swallow all keys. The unit test was rewritten to match. A button has no native Arrow/PageDown behavior, so nothing is literally double-handled. The spec's wording still reads as \"no deck advance\"."},{"line":556,"text":"- **Decision needed:** which behavior is intended for focused buttons and links?"},{"line":557,"text":" 1. Keep the current behavior and amend the spec/test-plan wording to \"Space/Enter activate the focused control; text-entry controls keep all keys\". Impact: keyboard nav survives mouse clicks on chrome. A keyboard user who tabs to a button and presses Arrow still moves the deck. The spec text must change."},{"line":558,"text":" 2. Revert to the literal spec: ignore all nav keys on any focused interactive control. Impact: matches the spec. After any mouse click on chrome, Arrow/Page keys do nothing until focus moves, which is the original complaint. Revert the test in `tests/navigation.test.tsx` too."},{"line":559,"text":" 3. Hybrid: keep the literal spec for keyboard-focused controls and blur (or avoid retaining focus on) chrome buttons after a pointer click. Impact: satisfies both, but adds new design work in the kit's chrome components and tests."},{"line":560,"text":"- **Note:** the same code is mirrored under `skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/`. That commit changed behavior away from the approved spec on the strength of a validator complaint, without a recorded user decision. When acceptance reproduced the violation, A1 was escalated as a three-way choice, and its first option is to keep the nonconforming behavior and amend the spec. Neither the findings nor the handoff records a defect, and the A1 escalation offers keeping the behavior as a valid outcome. Under the review guidance, a reproduced violation framed as a design choice fails this criterion. Judges A and B cite the options and the stated impacts as proportionate escalation. Offering options does not cure a reproduced, specified requirement violation that the record declines to treat as a defect. The appropriate response was to record it as a finding against the spec.","evidence":["Ledger line 554: the behavior came from commit 93386a2 &#39;[fix-violations]&#39;, which changed key handling contrary to the spec.","Ledger line 557, option 1: &#39;Keep the current behavior and amend the spec/test-plan wording.&#39;","Ledger line 590: &#39;choosing the intended behavior is a product/spec decision.&#39;","Ledger line 602: the reproduction confirms the deck advances with a focused progress button, yet the interpretation is left unresolved and no finding is recorded (findings line 689)."],"citations":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":32,"end_line":32},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":553,"end_line":561},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":590,"end_line":590},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":601,"end_line":602},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":685,"end_line":689},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":642,"end_line":644}],"search_scope":[],"missing_obligation":""}],"spans":{"assumption-repository-facts-distinguished":[{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":32,"end_line":32,"lines":[{"line":32,"text":" \"text\": \"## ADDED Requirements\\n\\n### Requirement: Scene step model\\nA presentation SHALL be one scene rendered through an ordered list of named steps. Each step SHALL have a stable identity, a section/era label, a presenter title (one-liner), a browse caption (paragraph), and a diagram state shown while it is active.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Step carries narration and identity\\n- **WHEN** a presentation defines a step\\n- **THEN** that step has a stable id, a section/era label, a presenter title, a browse caption, and the diagram state shown while it is active\\n\\n#### Scenario: Order-derived numbering\\n- **WHEN** steps are inserted, removed, or reordered\\n- **THEN** each step's on-screen number is derived from its position so no manual renumbering is required\\n\\n#### Scenario: Typed payloads reach presentation boundary\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene defines steps with a strongly typed payload\\n- **THEN** the presentation host accepts that typed step array without requiring casts at the `<Presentation>` boundary\\n\\n### Requirement: Stable entities morph across steps\\nEntities that persist between steps SHALL keep a stable identity and animate their change in place rather than disappearing and reappearing. Entities present in only one of two adjacent steps SHALL animate in or out.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Persisting entity morphs\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same identity exists in two consecutive steps\\n- **THEN** navigating between them animates that entity from its old state (position, size, label, emphasis) to its new state in place\\n\\n#### Scenario: New entity enters after others settle\\n- **WHEN** a step introduces a new entity\\n- **THEN** it animates in after the persisting entities have moved to their new positions\\n\\n#### Scenario: Departing entity exits\\n- **WHEN** an entity exists in a step but not in the next step\\n- **THEN** it animates out on that transition\\n\\n### Requirement: Persistent grouped scenes\\nAdjacent steps that represent successive states of the same evolving diagram SHALL be able to share a scene group so that the scene component persists while only the active step data changes. Shared groups prevent the whole scene from remounting between beats and preserve entity continuity for layout morphs.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Grouped steps update in place\\n- **WHEN** adjacent steps share a scene group and the same scene component\\n- **THEN** navigating between those steps updates the existing scene instance with the new step state rather than remounting separate scenes\\n\\n#### Scenario: Continuing entities are not faded as newcomers\\n- **WHEN** an entity with the same stable identity continues across grouped steps\\n- **THEN** it morphs through layout projection without being wrapped in newcomer fade-in behavior\\n\\n#### Scenario: Intentional composition is preserved\\n- **WHEN** a grouped scene intentionally overlaps or stacks entities\\n- **THEN** the implementation preserves that composition while maintaining clean morphs, rather than flattening or spreading entities only to satisfy an implementation pattern\\n\\n### Requirement: Style ownership boundary\\nThe scene kit SHALL have zero styling defaults. It SHALL provide motion behavior, fixed-canvas layout plumbing, navigation/chrome behavior, and stable DOM hooks for authors to style, but it SHALL NOT impose a palette, font, color, border treatment, glow, card appearance, button style, spacing scale, CSS theme tokens, or styling-framework dependency. Any default geometry used for the fixed canvas or chrome placement is layout behavior, not a visual style system.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Kit primitives expose style hooks\\n- **WHEN** a presentation composes scene kit primitives or chrome\\n- **THEN** the rendered markup exposes stable hooks that presentation-owned CSS can target\\n- **AND** visual choices such as color, typography, spacing scale, borders, and shadows come from the presentation or host app\\n\\n#### Scenario: Unstyled kit output\\n- **WHEN** a presentation uses scene kit primitives without presentation-owned CSS\\n- **THEN** the kit does not supply fallback colors, fonts, borders, shadows, card treatments, or button treatments\\n\\n#### Scenario: Optional styling frameworks remain optional\\n- **WHEN** a presentation author wants to use Tailwind or another styling framework\\n- **THEN** that framework is configured by the presentation or host app, not required by the reusable scene kit\\n\\n#### Scenario: Coordinate-heavy diagrams are supported\\n- **WHEN** a presentation needs literal per-step coordinates for diagram entities\\n- **THEN** kit primitives expose class/style hooks, and authors MAY use raw motion elements with stable `layoutId`s when a primitive is not the right shape\\n\\n### Requirement: Kit attribution\\nThe scene kit SHALL include a default attribution link reading \\\"made by and-scene\\\" in the bottom-right corner, linking to the and-scene GitHub repository. The attribution is toolkit disclosure, not a presentation style system. The kit SHALL expose a stable hook so presentation-owned CSS can make the attribution legible and intentional. The kit SHALL NOT add a default top-left \\\"and-scene\\\" brand link; host applications MAY provide their own header brand explicitly.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default attribution is shown\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without overriding attribution options\\n- **THEN** it shows a bottom-right link labeled \\\"made by and-scene\\\" pointing to the and-scene GitHub repository\\n\\n#### Scenario: Attribution exposes a styling hook\\n- **WHEN** the default attribution is rendered\\n- **THEN** it exposes a stable presentation hook that the presentation or host app can target for local styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Top-left brand is opt-in\\n- **WHEN** a presentation renders without host-provided branding\\n- **THEN** the top-left header slot does not contain a default and-scene brand link\\n\\n### Requirement: Present and browse modes\\nA presentation SHALL support a present mode for live delivery and a browse mode for self-guided reading, switchable at runtime, and MAY declare which mode it opens in.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Present mode is title-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in present mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its marker and one-line title, with the caption, table of contents, and prev/next controls hidden\\n\\n#### Scenario: Browse mode is reading-focused\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is in browse mode\\n- **THEN** the active step shows its title, multi-line caption, a table of contents on wide viewports, prev/next controls, and step progress indicators\\n\\n#### Scenario: Mode toggle preserves position\\n- **WHEN** the user toggles the mode\\n- **THEN** the presentation switches between present and browse while staying on the current step\\n\\n### Requirement: Step navigation\\nA presentation SHALL let the viewer move between steps via keyboard, touch, and on-screen controls, and SHALL allow jumping directly to a step or section.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Keyboard navigation\\n- **WHEN** the user presses Right, Space, or PageDown\\n- **THEN** the presentation advances one step; and WHEN the user presses Left or PageUp THEN it goes back one step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Touch swipe\\n- **WHEN** the user swipes horizontally\\n- **THEN** swiping left advances and swiping right goes back\\n\\n#### Scenario: Direct jump\\n- **WHEN** the user activates a progress indicator or a table-of-contents entry\\n- **THEN** the presentation jumps directly to that step, or to the first step of that section's era for a table-of-contents entry\\n\\n#### Scenario: Active navigation state is exposed\\n- **WHEN** a progress indicator or table-of-contents entry represents the active step\\n- **THEN** it exposes semantic current-step state and a stable active-state hook for presentation-owned styling\\n\\n#### Scenario: Controls keep their keys\\n- **WHEN** focus is on an interactive control\\n- **THEN** navigation keys drive that control rather than also advancing the deck\\n\\n### Requirement: Boundary behavior\\nNavigation SHALL clamp at both ends with no wrap-around.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at start\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the first step and the user goes back\\n- **THEN** it stays on the first step\\n\\n#### Scenario: Clamp at end\\n- **WHEN** the presentation is on the last step and the user advances\\n- **THEN** it stays on the last step\\n\\n### Requirement: Fixed-canvas fit scaling\\nThe diagram SHALL be composed in a fixed design canvas and scaled uniformly to fit the available viewport, so the composition does not reflow and entity morphs stay clean across viewport sizes. The default design canvas SHALL be 880 × 380, with per-mode fit geometry for the browse and present layouts.\\n\\n#### Scenario: Uniform scaling on resize\\n- **WHEN** the viewport size changes\\n- **THEN** the diagram scales uniformly to fit without reflowing its internal composition\\n\\n#### Scenario: Default canvas dimensions\\n- **WHEN** a presentation does not override the design canvas\\n- **THEN** it uses the default dimensions of 880 × 380\\n\""}],"label":"[harness frame or verified index]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":553,"end_line":561,"lines":[{"line":553,"text":"### A1. Arrow/PageUp/PageDown keys advance the deck while a button or link has focus (risky)"},{"line":554,"text":"- **Source:** session report, risky assumption 1; `src/presentation-kit/usePresentationNav.ts:14-17`, commit `93386a2` (`[fix-violations]`)."},{"line":555,"text":"- **Why undecided:** the spec scenario \"Controls keep their keys\" (`evolving-scene-presentations/spec.md`) says that with focus on an interactive control, navigation keys drive that control and do not also advance the deck. The `test-plan.md` AT-003 step repeats this (\"without double-handling focused-control keys\"). A validator finding pointed the other way: after clicking a progress dot, Next/Prev or a ToC entry, the button keeps focus and every nav key is ignored, so keyboard navigation looks broken. The fix lets Arrow/PageUp/PageDown through on buttons, links and `[role=button]`. Only Space and Enter are left to the control. Text inputs, textareas, selects and contenteditable elements still swallow all keys. The unit test was rewritten to match. A button has no native Arrow/PageDown behavior, so nothing is literally double-handled. The spec's wording still reads as \"no deck advance\"."},{"line":556,"text":"- **Decision needed:** which behavior is intended for focused buttons and links?"},{"line":557,"text":" 1. Keep the current behavior and amend the spec/test-plan wording to \"Space/Enter activate the focused control; text-entry controls keep all keys\". Impact: keyboard nav survives mouse clicks on chrome. A keyboard user who tabs to a button and presses Arrow still moves the deck. The spec text must change."},{"line":558,"text":" 2. Revert to the literal spec: ignore all nav keys on any focused interactive control. Impact: matches the spec. After any mouse click on chrome, Arrow/Page keys do nothing until focus moves, which is the original complaint. Revert the test in `tests/navigation.test.tsx` too."},{"line":559,"text":" 3. Hybrid: keep the literal spec for keyboard-focused controls and blur (or avoid retaining focus on) chrome buttons after a pointer click. Impact: satisfies both, but adds new design work in the kit's chrome components and tests."},{"line":560,"text":"- **Note:** the same code is mirrored under `skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/src/presentation-kit/`. Any change must be applied to both copies."},{"line":561,"text":""}],"label":"[artifact candidate-39e6f4ae8dc8dde2 (assumptions-ledger)]"},{"path":"packet.txt","start_line":590,"end_line":590,"lines":[{"line":590,"text":"- Existing unresolved assumption A1 remains: navigation key handling while buttons or links have focus does not match the literal spec wording, and choosing the intended behavior is a product/spec decision. The approved spec scenario &#39;Controls keep their keys&#39; says that when focus is on an interactive control, navigation keys drive that control &#39;rather than also advancing the deck&#39;. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[{"id":"demo-scope-discipline","classification":"confirmed","rationale":"For demo-scope-discipline, the review guidance says to fail when the inspected architecture shows &quot;duplicated shared mechanisms&quot;. It builds `reveal-frame` and `reveal-label` by hand as `motion.div layout layoutId={entity(...)} data-presentation-entity={entity(...)}`, which copies the shared Frame and Label mechanism instead of using it. The hand-built versions also drop the kit&#39;s `data-presentation-frame` and `data-presentation-label` markers. The parts of the pass that are correct (local registry entry, Talk delegating to Presentation, Stage hosting) do not undo this, because the guidance treats duplicated shared mechanisms as a separate fail condition. The duplication sits in the presentation-local implementation and against the shared kit boundary, both of which the guidance says to inspect.
